page: Microsoft Azure DC8es_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, powered by a dedicated 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon processor featuring Trust Domain Extensions (TDX). It allocates 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled at two threads per core, combined with 32.0 GB of system memory. This yields a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The underlying CPU incorporates a 260 MB L3 cache, a 2 MB L2 cache, and extended instruction sets such as AVX-512, AMX-TILE, and AMX-INT8, alongside cryptographic acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent average-tier performance across general compute suites. In stress-ng, the instance achieves 1,717.18 points in single-core and 7,011.03 points in multi-core metrics, while Geekbench results yield 1,855.0 and 7,602.0, respectively. Text processing in Geekbench registers in the top 25% at 2,509.0 points. In-memory data handling is highlighted by a throughput of 8.32 million SET operations per second in Redis and a PassMark database operations rating of 4,846.25. The server bundles neither local ephemeral disk storage nor dedicated GPUs, requiring network-attached storage for all filesystem activity.

The absence of bundled local storage reduces operational overhead for workloads that do not need scratch disks, focusing cost efficiency on dedicated CPU cycles and system memory. The DC8es_v6 is well suited for containerized microservices, middle-tier enterprise web backends, caching services, and database layers integrated with cloud block storage.
description: Microsoft Azure DC8es_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon TDX processor operating at 4.2 GHz. Running on Microsoft Hyper-V, it is provisioned with 8 dedicated vCPUs spanning 4 physical cores, paired with 32.0 GB of memory to yield a standard 1:4 core-to-memory allocation. The processor incorporates a 260 MB L3 cache alongside hardware support for AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions. Lacking local ephemeral storage and physical GPU hardware, the VM depends on remote storage solutions. In benchmark testing, the DC8es_v6 demonstrates consistent average multi-core and single-core compute performance, alongside strong text processing output in Geekbench and 8.32 million Redis SET operations per second. Its balanced footprint delivers cost-effective dedicated compute capacity for containerized microservices, middle-tier enterprise web serving, and database workloads backed by networked block storage.
